column1: # redundancy-precision-labels.tsv — the hand-labelled precision sample for the
# P9 semantic-redundancy probe (temperloop#855, half (b); epic #810).
# WHAT THIS IS. workflows/scripts/score-redundancy.sh ranks every chunk pair
# over the always-loaded surface by duplicated-byte weight. This file carries a
# human verdict on the TOP `REDUNDANCY_LABEL_SAMPLE_N` of that ranking; the
# script joins it back on by pair id and reports precision = TP / labelled,
# with the sample size stated beside the figure. Without this file there is no
# precision figure — only a ranking.
# THE LABELLING PROTOCOL IS PRE-REGISTERED, NOT CHOSEN HERE. Every verdict
# below applies workflows/scripts/score-redundancy.md § Pre-registration PR-5,
# which was committed BEFORE this detector existed and before any pair over the
# real surface had been scored. Its rule, in one line: a pair is a TRUE POSITIVE
# iff (1) the overlapping portion states the same rule/constraint/fact in both
# chunks, and (2) a maintainer could cut that content from one member — outright
# or by replacing it with a reference to the other — without the surface losing
# anything it carries today. PR-5 also disposes, in advance, the four recurring
# hard cases (deliberate pointer; same subject different rule; shared frame with
# differing slots; adjacent chunks of one continued thought), so none of them was
# decided after a number was visible. Do not re-derive a verdict here — apply
# PR-5, and if PR-5 does not settle a case, that is a gap to record in the doc,
# not a judgment call to make silently in this file.
#   id_a<TAB>id_b<TAB>tp|fp<TAB>rationale
# id_a / id_b  chunk ids exactly as chunk-redundancy-surface.sh emits them
#              (`<path>#<chunk_index>`). Order is irrelevant — the scorer keys
#              on the unordered pair.
# tp | fp      the PR-5 verdict. tp = genuine redundancy the detector found;
#              fp = the detector flagged something that is not redundancy.
# rationale    one line, mandatory in practice: it is what makes the precision
#              figure auditable rather than a bare ratio.
# A pair id can go stale when the surface changes (a chunk index shifts, a
# description is reworded). The scorer reports a labelled pair that is no
# longer in the top-N in an explicit STALE LABELS bucket and excludes it from
# the figure — it never silently counts a stale row, and never treats an
# UNLABELLED top-N pair as a true positive.
# The 12 rows below are the top 12 candidates by duplicated-byte weight as
# ranked on 2026-08-02 against the surface at that commit. They were labelled in
# one pass, in rank order, before the precision figure was computed.
